name: GlucoTwin twin-validity protocol, addendum v2 (post-hoc / exploratory)
status: POST-HOC. Written after the v1 results (reports/research/twin_validity.json) were known. Nothing in this addendum replaces or re-scores a v1 analysis; v1 results are collated unchanged.
scope: Synthetic simulator cohort only (seed 20261017, 60 patients x 14 days, split 36/12/12). Frozen served models; no retraining, no change to served behaviour. Not clinical evidence.
simulator: src/glucotwin/synth/generator.py, documented there as 'an extended Bergman minimal model integrated with 1-minute Euler'. Ground-truth meal effects come from paired runs with common random numbers (glucotwin.twin_validity_research.paired_meal_delta), exactly as in v1.

A_post_meal.question: Does personalisation help in post-meal windows, where it should matter most?
A_post_meal.rows: Test-split feature rows with carbs_60 >= 10 g (at least 10 g of logged carbohydrate in the 60 min before the forecast moment) and an observed target.
A_post_meal.arms: served = frozen trajectory model on the served features; ablated = same model with carb_sensitivity set to the day-0 EHR prior and expected_meal_rise recomputed from it (identical to v1 analysis A).
A_post_meal.contrast: ablated minus served (positive = personalisation helps), paired patient bootstrap CI

B_grams.question: Does the served What-If track true counterfactual deltas across meal sizes outside the preset range?
B_grams.anchors: the same 32 replay offsets x 12 test patients as v1 B
B_grams.eligibility: identical to v1 B: latest CGM <= 180 mg/dL, forecast not withheld, joint-support status within_training_support. Counts excluded per gram are reported.
B_grams.truth: simulator paired delta at the service's own anchor minute
B_grams.baseline: cohort average: mean true delta per (grams, horizon) over training patients at eligible anchors (latest CGM <= 180), as in v1
B_grams.contrast: served What-If minus baseline for MAE and for median AE, paired patient bootstrap CI

C_exploratory_observed_curve.status: EXPLORATORY research estimator; not served, not a product claim.
C_exploratory_observed_curve.question: Could a personalised response curve learned only from observed CGM beat the cohort-average baseline?
C_exploratory_observed_curve.curve: For every meal in training patients that glucotwin.features.meal_responses accepts (isolated, >= 10 g, >= 50% window observed), take observed rise at h = CGM(tm + h) - last CGM at or before tm, divided by that meal's observed peak rise (ratio x carbs). Use meals with peak rise >= 5 mg/dL. c(h) = median of that fraction. Observed CGM only; simulator truth is never used to fit it.
C_exploratory_observed_curve.estimator_personal: delta_hat(h) = grams x s(patient, anchor) x c(h), where s is glucotwin.features.personal_carb_sensitivity at the anchor time (shrunk running mean, k = 3, using only meals whose available_at <= anchor).
C_exploratory_observed_curve.estimator_cohort_curve: delta_hat(h) = grams x S x c(h), with S = median observed ratio across training meals (isolates the effect of personalisation).
C_exploratory_observed_curve.evaluation: same eligible scenarios and grams as B_grams plus the v1 preset grams (25, 35, 36, 45, 50) scored against the same truth and baseline
C_exploratory_observed_curve.contrast: estimator_personal minus baseline MAE at 30/60/120 min, paired patient bootstrap CI

analyses.collate_v1: Copy v1 A, A2 (r, rho, MAE by day) and B by_horizon unchanged from reports/research/twin_validity.json.

reporting_rules: Report every pre-specified number, including null and negative results.
Do not change definitions after seeing results; any deviation is listed under deviations in the output.
Direction accuracy is uninformative when all true deltas share a sign; report the sign distribution next to it.
